title: Packing k^2-c unit squares: a lower bound of order k^{1/4} for the deficiency (preprint)
description: Licences in this single record: the preprint (paper/paper.pdf, paper/paper.tex) is licensed under CC BY 4.0; the programs (code/) under the MIT License, which is the licence shown for the record. Preprint with programs. Every packing of N unit squares in [0,k]^2 that are pairwise disjoint as closed sets has k^2 - N >= 0.1 k^{1/4} for every integer k >= 4.62*10^12, and liminf (k^2 - M(k))/k^{1/4} >= 0.1696; consequently s(k^2-c) = k for every integer k >= max(4.62*10^12, 10^4 c^4 + 1), where s(n) is the side of the smallest square containing n non-overlapping unit squares. The constants 0.1, 4.62*10^12 and 0.1696 rely on the computer-assisted Lemma 4.10 of the cited paper (Packing k^2-c unit squares: s(k^2-c)=k for all large k, version 1.2), whose box computations have not yet been reproduced by an independent implementation; without it, using the analytic Lemma 4.9 of that paper, the same argument gives k^2 - N >= 0.1 k^{1/4} for every integer k >= 2.17*10^13 and the constant 0.1411. The threshold 4.62*10^12 has a small margin: with the parameters of the proof the argument works exactly from about 4.6167*10^12 on. Includes a script that recomputes every displayed constant and the programs and results of numerical tests on scaled analogues (tests, not part of the proof). Status: checked only by AI-based reviews (including a blank-slate review of this text: no critical or major issue, 18 minor ones, all addressed) and numerical tests; not peer reviewed. Use of AI: developed with extensive assistance from Claude (Anthropic), including the proofs, the text and the programs; the author takes full responsibility.
